title: The Lost Current
premise: Storm chaser Ines Vasquez, drowning in debt to the Delgado brothers' cheerful loan syndicate, accepts a dying prospector's map in exchange for a promise to deliver it to his estranged daughter. The map points to a river that vanishes underground for twenty miles — and reappears carrying gold dust from an unmapped source. Racing the Delgados, a rival survey crew, and the seasons themselves across a mountain range that demands she beat both the early snows and the monsoon, Ines discovers the prospector's daughter is not who anyone claims, and that the 'lost current' is a lie built on a drowned town. In the end, Ines chooses truth over the fortune: she exposes the source as unstable floodland, burns the map, pays her debt with the only salvage worth anything — the truth of what happened to the town — and finally measures her life in years instead of miles.
about_author: Marguerite Ravensworth is the pen name of a former field hydrologist who spent a decade mapping seasonal rivers across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels where landscapes are characters and every promise has a price.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Ines Vasquez chases a supercell across the high plains, measuring her life in odometer readings while dodging calls from the Delgado brothers about her mounting debt. When they corner her at a roadside diner with a 'generous' final extension, she takes any job offered. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: restless denial — a woman outrunning consequences at seventy miles an hour.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: A prospector named Elias Crane collapses at Ines's campsite, radiation of old ambition in his eyes, and trades her a hand-drawn map for one promise: deliver it to his daughter, Marisol, in the mountain town of Puerto Cielo. He dies by morning. The Delgados, having followed him, learn of the map. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: reluctant obligation hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Cheerful Creditors
chapters.summary: The Delgados offer to 'partner' on the expedition, their optimism more frightening than threats. Ines stalls, then slips out of town at dawn with her mechanic friend Bo, who insists on coming. They realize they're being tailed by a second vehicle — a corporate survey crew led by the polished Halloran. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Marisol
chapters.summary: Ines finds Marisol Crane running a failing hostel in Puerto Cielo — and discovers she already has a map, a different one, given by a man claiming to be Elias's partner. Marisol doesn't trust Ines; worse, she doesn't seem to want the inheritance at all. POV: alternating Ines and Marisol. Emotional beat: suspicion between two women who both loved the same liar.

chapters.title: The Range Ahead of the Snows
chapters.summary: The four of them — Ines, Bo, Marisol, and Marisol's taciturn guide Tomás — enter the mountains as weather satellites show an early cold front. The Delgados follow with hired muscle; Halloran's crew takes the southern pass. A rockslide forces an alliance of necessity. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into focus; the race becomes real.

chapters.title: What the River Remembers
chapters.summary: Tomás reveals local history: fifty years ago the town of Agua Perdida was flooded by a dam project that officially never existed, its survivors scattered and silenced. The 'gold' in the lost current may be washed from the drowned valley. Marisol goes quiet — her mother was born there. POV: Marisol. Emotional beat: grief surfacing through anger.

chapters.title: Halloran's Offer
chapters.summary: Halloran catches them at a high camp and makes a clean offer: sell the map, split the find, everyone walks away rich and alive. Ines is tempted — it would erase her debt. Bo warns her the survey crew's permits don't exist. That night someone searches their gear. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: temptation versus loyalty; the first true moral fork.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Makes Landfall
chapters.summary: The monsoon arrives weeks early, swallowing the lower passes. The Delgados, desperate, force a confrontation on a rope bridge; Bo is injured covering Ines's escape, and the bridge — and the Delgados' claim — goes into the gorge. Ines reaches the source alone: not gold, but a valley poised to fail catastrophically when the rains peak. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into horror.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Climax. Ines races back to warn the others as the saturated slope above Agua Perdida begins to move. Halloran's crew refuses to leave without samples; Marisol chooses to stay and help evacuate a herder family living in the old flood zone. Ines uses her storm-chasing instincts to read the mountain like weather, timing their escape to the minute. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: courage as calculation — everything she's learned finally meaning something.

chapters.title: Years, Not Miles
chapters.summary: The slope fails behind them; the lost current runs red with silt, its secret buried deeper than ever. Halloran is arrested when his forged permits surface; the Delgados, ruined, vanish. Ines settles her debt honestly, stays a season in Puerto Cielo helping Marisol rebuild the hostel, and for the first time unpacks her bags completely. POV: Ines. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — a woman who measured life in miles learning to count years instead.
